The Department of Fisheries, Government of India organized a
National Workshop on Promotion of Deep-Sea Fishing and Interaction with Access Pass Holders
on
17th September 2026
in
Gandhinagar, Gujarat
. The National workshop aims to promote deep-sea fishing by encouraging fishers to harness high-value fisheries resources, while also providing a platform to understand on-ground challenges and gather stakeholder suggestions for further strengthening the sector. Department of Fisheries, Government of India has given special thrust to strengthening fisheries farmer producer organizations (FFPO) and fisheries cooperatives while also focusing on digitization of the fisheries sector through various initiatives.
The National workshop was graced by presence of Shri Bhupendrabhai Patel, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Gujarat; Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh, Hon’ble Union Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying and Panchayati Raj; along with Prof. S. P. Singh Baghel, Hon’ble Minister of State for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying and Panchayati Raj. The event also witnessed participation form fishers including women fishers in person, along with officials from the Department of Fisheries, GoI, Government of Gujarat, ICAR, INCOIS, CIFNET, ASCI, NABARD, NCEL, NCDC, SEAI, MPEDA, EIC and other fisheries stakeholders.
Shri Bhupendrabhai Patel
, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Gujarat, highlighted Gujarat’s unique advantage of having the country’s longest coastline and urged fishers to fully leverage the opportunities being created through the Government of India’s deep-sea fishing initiatives. He emphasized that Gujarat stands to benefit significantly from investments in deep-sea fishing, training, infrastructure and market access, and assured the fishing community of the State Government’s full support in facilitating participation in training and capacity-building programmes. The Chief Minister encouraged fishers to proactively avail themselves of the benefits being offered by the Central and State Governments, particularly in areas such as skill development, cold-chain infrastructure and cooperative-led initiatives. He noted that the State Government is ready to support the establishment of cold storage facilities and facilitate training opportunities to help fishers enhance value realization from marine resources. Stressing the importance of collective efforts, he called upon all stakeholders to work together to harness Gujarat’s vast marine potential, strengthen the fisheries sector and contribute to the vision of a developed Gujarat and a developed India by 2047.
Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh
, Hon’ble Union Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying and Panchayati Raj, highlighted the transformative growth of India's fisheries sector under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi through various schemes and initiatives. He noted that fish production has increased to a record
197.75 lakh tonnes in 2024-25, while seafood exports have more than doubled. The Minister pointed out that despite global trade barriers and increased tariffs in key markets, India’s seafood exports rose by ₹11,400 crore to a record ₹73,890 crore, reflecting the sector’s growing resilience and global competitiveness.
The Minister emphasized that the objective of issuing
Access Passes for fishing in the EEZ and Letters of Authorisation for High Seas Fishing
is to enable fishers to tap the vast untapped potential of high-value resources such as
tuna and other oceanic species
, increase exports and enhance incomes. He urged fishers to move beyond traditional fishing grounds, target high-value species in the EEZ and high seas, and adopt modern fishing practices supported by onboard processing, cold-chain infrastructure, value addition, branding and export-oriented market linkages. Stressing the importance of skill development and technology adoption, he called upon states to prepare structured training roadmaps for fishers and encouraged stakeholders to leverage concessional financing available under FIDF. He also noted that the fee for obtaining a
Letter of Authorisation for High Seas Fishing has been reduced from ₹25,000 to ₹5,000 for cooperative societies
, making it easier for fisher collectives to participate in deep-sea fishing and contribute to the growth of India's Blue Economy.
During the event
Prof. S.P. Singh Baghel
, Minister of State for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying and Panchayati Raj, highlighted that the workshop had provided a valuable platform for deliberations on deep-sea fishing, covering issues such as technology adoption, cold-chain infrastructure, value addition, processing, market access and export opportunities. He shed light on the transformative impact of the Government’s initiatives in the fisheries sector, particularly the creation of a dedicated Department of Fisheries, the launch of PMMSY, and the promotion of the Blue Revolution and Blue Economy, which have contributed to increased fish production, productivity, exports and employment generation. He noted that the issuance of access passes is enabling fishers to venture into deeper waters and tap high-value resources, particularly tuna, thereby creating new opportunities for income enhancement and export growth. He emphasized that strengthening the entire fisheries value chain, including infrastructure, processing, value addition and market linkages, would be key to realizing the full potential of India’s marine fisheries sector and advancing the vision of a vibrant Blue Economy.
Dr. Abhilaksh Likhi
, Secretary (Fisheries), Department of Fisheries, emphasized that India's deep-sea fisheries potential can only be fully realized through the active participation of fishers, cooperatives, FPOs, self-help groups and women stakeholders. He highlighted the immense opportunities in high-value oceanic resources such as tuna and stressed the need for modern fishing vessels, advanced technologies, sustainable fishing practices, capacity building and skill development to enhance fishers' incomes and strengthen the competitiveness of the marine fisheries sector. Reflecting on the discussions held during the workshop, he identified
training and capacity building, improved access to finance, and the strengthening of cooperative institutions
as the three key priorities for promoting deep-sea fishing. He assured the participants that the feedback and suggestions received from fishers and stakeholders would be incorporated into policy and programme implementation to accelerate the sustainable growth of India's deep-sea fisheries sector and improve livelihoods across fishing communities.
During the interaction with Letter of Authorisation (LoA) and Access Pass holders, fishers widely appretiated the Government’s decision to issue access passes, noting that it had enabled them to venture beyond traditional nearshore fishing grounds into the EEZ, opening up new opportunities to target high-value species such as tuna and other oceanic resources. Participants observed that access to deeper fishing grounds had improved livelihood prospects and created opportunities for higher incomes through export-oriented fisheries. The fishers also highlighted the need for enhanced support in the form of training on quality handling and value addition, cold-chain and cold storage infrastructure at fishing harbours, modernization of deep-sea fishing vessels, improved communication systems, and greater financial assistance for deep-sea fishing operations. They emphasized that strengthening these ecosystem enablers would help maximize the benefits of access passes, improve price realization, and unlock the full potential of India’s deep-sea fisheries sector.
The workshop featured five technical sessions covering the entire deep-sea fisheries value chain, including sustainable utilization of oceanic resources, modernization of fishing vessels, adoption of advanced technologies, capacity building, financing mechanisms, value addition, traceability systems, and export market access. The themes included Unlocking India’s Blue Economy: Deep-Sea Fishing Opportunities in the EEZ and High Seas for Enhanced Seafood Exports, Transforming India’s Deep-Sea Fishing Fleet- Modern Vessel Technologies and Global Best Practices, Building a Future-Ready Deep-Sea Fishing Workforce- Specialized Training, Skills and Capacity Development, Financing Mechanisms for Deep-Sea Fishing and From Deep-Sea Catch to Global Markets - Processing, Value Addition, Traceability and Export Compliance. Across five technical sessions, 19 speakers comprising experts from government, research institutions, financial institutions, industry, international organizations and fisher representatives deliberated.
The speakers collectively emphasized that India has significant untapped potential in deep-sea fisheries, particularly for high-value species such as tuna, squid asnd other oceanic resources. They highlighted the need to shift fishing activities beyond nearshore waters through modern vessels, advanced fishing technologies, cold-chain infrastructure, scientific fish handling, traceability systems and international certification to improve fishers' incomes, seafood exports and overall value realization. Shri R. Ravindra, Ambassador of India to Iceland
,
shared Iceland's best practices in advanced fishing vessels, automated onboard processing, electronic monitoring and sustainable fisheries management, while advocating a "whole-of-fish" approach for maximizing value.
The discussions further underscored the importance of skill development, practical training, affordable financing, cooperative-led investments, modern harbour infrastructure, communication and safety systems, processing and value addition, digital catch documentation, export compliance and market access. Stakeholders and fisher representatives stressed that strengthening capacity building, improving access to credit, enhancing infrastructure, and adopting fisher-friendly digital traceability platforms would be critical for enabling fishers to successfully transition to deep-sea fishing and unlocking the full potential of India's Blue Economy.
The deliberations served as a significant platform for strengthening India’s deep-sea fishing ecosystem by bringing together policymakers, technical experts, financial institutions, industry stakeholders, cooperatives, and fishers for focused deliberations. The discussions and recommendations emerging from the workshop will help identify practical solutions to on-ground challenges, improve access to technology, skills, finance, and markets, and facilitate greater participation of fishers in deep-sea fishing.

The Minister listened to their experiences and enquired about the impact of government support on their businesses and livelihoods, including the employment opportunities generated through their projects.
Food processing: a major opportunity
The programme also highlighted the immense potential of the food-processing sector. While India once faced limitations in food production, the country today has a strong and diverse agricultural production base, creating significant scope for processing, preservation and value addition.
The need of the hour is therefore to give greater impetus to food processing and build a strong and integrated value chain that connects farmers, FPOs, entrepreneurs, processors, industry and markets.
The emerging participation of entrepreneurs from both rural and urban India reflects this changing landscape. Entrepreneurs from different backgrounds are increasingly coming forward to establish food-processing enterprises and build products that represent the spirit of Brand Bharat.

Beneficiaries shared their experiences and explained how government initiatives had helped them strengthen their enterprises, create employment and move towards greater economic self-reliance.

The programme reinforced the message of Seva Sankalp Abhiyan–Seva Diwas—that the true purpose of public service is realised when opportunities created through government initiatives reach people and translate into enterprise, employment, value addition and better livelihoods.
The “Aashirwad Ka Diya” thus became a symbol of a larger vision: to transform India’s agricultural strength into greater value, stronger enterprises and new opportunities, while carrying the light of entrepreneurship and self-reliance to more families across the country.

title: Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission inaugurates 6th National Pharmacovigilance Week with focus on rational use of medicines
subtitle:
6th National Pharmacovigilance Week to be observed across the country from 17–23 September 2026  

Week-long campaign to sensitise healthcare professionals, researchers and public on Adverse Drug Reaction (ADR) reporting and encourage active participation in pharmacovigilance
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                17 SEP 2026 10:11PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The 6th National Pharmacovigilance Week (NPW) was inaugurated at the Padmashri Nitya Anand Auditorium Hall, ALRC Building, Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission (IPC), Ghaziabad, today.  IPC serves as the National Coordination Centre for the Pharmacovigilance Programme of India (NCC-PvPI). Being observed from 17–23 September 2026 across the country, the 6th NPW is themed “Promoting Rational Use of Medicines through Pharmacovigilance – A Step Towards Safer Healthcare”. The week-long campaign aims to sensitise healthcare professionals, researchers and the public about the importance of adverse drug reaction (ADR) reporting and encourage active participation in pharmacovigilance.
The inaugural ceremony was attended by Dr. Rajiv Bahl, Director General, ICMR (virtually); Dr. V. Kalaiselvan, Secretary-cum-Scientific Director, IPC; Dr. Jai Prakash, Officer-in-Charge, PvPI; Prof. Sangeeta Sharma, IHBAS; Shri Aditya Kumar Mamgain, Deputy Secretary, MoHFW; and along with other dignitaries and stakeholders.
Dr. Rajiv Bahl, Director General, Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), stressed the importance of building adequate capacity to verify, assess and analyse safety reports, enabling pharmacovigilance data to effectively inform regulatory and clinical actions.
Dr. V. Kalaiselvan, Secretary-cum-Scientific Director, Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission, Ghaziabad, in his remarks, highlighted the need to strengthen the pharmacovigilance network at the grassroots level, with an aspiration for every Aspirational District to have at least one ADR Monitoring Centre (AMC) and one Medical Device Monitoring Centre (MDMC). He also emphasised greater utilisation of pharmacovigilance data, including exploring opportunities for drug repurposing and using safety data to support and promote the rational use of medicines.
The inaugural session also featured remarks by Prof. Sangeeta Sharma, Institute of Human Behaviour & Allied Sciences (IHBAS), New Delhi; Dr. Abdul Nasser, Cardiac Anaesthesiologist, Max Hospital, Vaishali; and Shri Aditya Kumar Mamgain, Deputy Secretary, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Government of India. Video messages were delivered by Shri Tukaram Mundhe, Commissioner, FDA Maharashtra and Dr. Shanthi Pal, Team Lead, Pharmacovigilance, World Health Organization (WHO).
A key highlight of the programme was the release of Volume 16, Issue 2 (2026) of the PvPI Newsletter, reflecting the programme’s continued efforts towards strengthening pharmacovigilance, promoting rational medicine use and enhancing public awareness on medicine safety.
The technical sessions focused on strengthening medication and patient safety. Prof. Sangeeta Sharma spoke on
“Pharmacovigilance and Rational Use of Medicines: Two Pillars of Medication Safety”
, while Dr. Abdul Nasser addressed
“Beyond Medicines: Role of MvPI in Strengthening Patient Safety”
, highlighting the complementary role of pharmacovigilance and materiovigilance.
The 6th NPW reinforces the call for greater ADR reporting and the effective use of pharmacovigilance data to promote safer and rational use of medicines.

title: Union Health Minister J.P. Nadda Addresses World Patient Safety Day 2026 Event at Dr. RML Hospital
subtitle:
Ayushman Bharat Has Enabled 11.5 Crore Beneficiaries to Access Treatment Worth Around ₹1.6 Lakh Crore: Union Health Minister

Jan Aushadhi Has Enabled Citizens to Save Around ₹45,000 Crore on Medicines: Shri Nadda

A Clean Hospital is Also a Safer Hospital: Union Health Minister J.P. Nadda on World Patient Safety Day

Quality & Safety Handbook Released at RML Hospital to Strengthen Patient Safety Practices
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                17 SEP 2026 9:34PM by PIB Delhi
content:
On the occasion of World Patient Safety Day 2026, Union Minister for Health & Family Welfare Shri J.P. Nadda addressed an event organised at Atal Bihari Vajpayee Institute of Medical Sciences (ABVIMS) & Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital, New Delhi, today. The event highlighted the Government’s continued efforts towards strengthening patient safety as an integral component of quality healthcare and health-system strengthening.
The theme for World Patient Safety Day 2026,
“Safe care for noncommunicable diseases”
, with the slogan
“Safe care for life!”
, highlights the importance of safe, coordinated and continuous care for people living with noncommunicable diseases (NCDs).
Addressing the gathering, Union Minister for Health & Family Welfare Shri J.P. Nadda said that 17 September is a significant day as it brings together the themes of public service, patient safety and cleanliness. He also conveyed his greetings and best wishes to Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on his birthday, noting that the occasion is an opportunity to acknowledge his contribution to public service and his continued commitment to the service of the nation. He expressed his wishes for the Prime Minister’s long, healthy life and continued service to the country.
Speaking on World Patient Safety Day, Shri Nadda said that patient safety is an extremely important component of healthcare and that the objective of healthcare delivery must extend beyond treatment to ensuring that every patient receives safe, high-quality, dignified and patient-centric care. He appreciated ABVIMS & Dr. RML Hospital for organising the programme and particularly commended the institution for bringing out the Quality & Safety Handbook, which provides a practical framework for strengthening quality and safety practices.
The Union Minister emphasised that patient safety requires the collective efforts of doctors, nurses, paramedical professionals, technicians, administrative personnel and other healthcare workers, along with patients and their attendants. He noted that safety and security of patients must remain central to healthcare delivery and that necessary precautions and protocols should not be compromised in the interest of speed. He stressed the importance of correct diagnosis, appropriate treatment, adherence to infection-prevention protocols and continuous attention to infection control.
Shri Nadda said that patient safety is closely linked with cleanliness and hygiene in healthcare facilities. Referring to the Swachhata movement, he highlighted the transformation of cleanliness into a people’s movement and emphasised that cleanliness should become a part of everyday habits and working practices. He noted that the creation of around 11 crore toilets over the past decade has significantly strengthened the country’s sanitation infrastructure and also contributed to dignity and improved living conditions.
The Union Minister said that the improvement in sanitation has also had an important bearing on public health outcomes, including a significant decline in diarrhoeal disease. He stressed that in hospitals, cleanliness has a direct connection with infection prevention and patient safety. He called for collective responsibility towards hand hygiene, proper waste disposal, adherence to infection-control protocols and maintaining hospital premises and facilities responsibly. He emphasised that a clean hospital is not merely a well-maintained hospital, but also a safer hospital.
Highlighting the importance of institutional quality assurance, Shri Nadda said that the National Quality Assurance Standards (NQAS) certification was introduced in 2015 to establish nationally recognised standards for assessing the quality of healthcare institutions. He noted that 60,000 government health facilities are now NQAS-certified and said that efforts are underway to further increase the number of certified institutions, with a target of taking the coverage to around 2 lakh institutions. He emphasised that the expansion of quality standards and certification reflects the continued focus on institutionalising quality, safety and patient-centric care across the public health system.
Shri Nadda also highlighted the role of Ayushman Bharat in strengthening financial protection and access to healthcare. He said that under the scheme, eligible beneficiaries are provided health coverage of up to ₹5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care. He said that Ayushman Bharat has emerged as one of the world’s largest health coverage programmes and has enabled millions of people to access treatment without facing the burden of catastrophic healthcare expenditure.
The Union Minister stated that approximately 11.5 crore beneficiaries have received treatment under Ayushman Bharat, with treatment worth of around ₹1.6 lakh crore. He said that the programme has enabled families, including elderly citizens, to access procedures and treatments that might otherwise have imposed a substantial financial burden on them.
Highlighting the role of the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP), Shri Nadda said that the initiative has expanded access to quality generic medicines at affordable prices. He noted that more than 20,000 Jan Aushadhi Kendras have been established across the country and that efforts are underway to expand this network further to around 25,000 outlets, while also increasing the range of medicines and ensuring their timely availability and quality. He also highlighted the substantial savings available on certain cancer medicines and said that the cumulative savings to citizens through Jan Aushadhi have been estimated at around ₹45,000 crore.
Shri Nadda further highlighted the importance of reducing out-of-pocket expenditure on healthcare. He noted that the share of out-of-pocket expenditure in total health expenditure has declined from around 62 per cent in 2014 to around 43 per cent, and emphasised that continued efforts are being made to reduce the financial burden on families.
The Union Minister also highlighted the importance of preventive healthcare, early detection and continuity of care. He referred to the strengthening of vaccination, maternal and child health services and screening for noncommunicable diseases. He noted that vaccination is being digitally tracked from childhood and that mechanisms are in place to ensure follow-up with beneficiaries and families so that due vaccinations are completed.
Shri Nadda said that screening and early detection of noncommunicable diseases are also being strengthened through the public health system. He highlighted screening for conditions including diabetes, hypertension and various cancers, including oral, cervical and breast cancer, and said that tens of crores of people have been screened under the ongoing efforts.
Emphasising the broader meaning of patient safety, Shri Nadda said that patients entering a hospital bring not only an illness but also anxiety, hope and expectations. He noted that the conduct of healthcare personnel—including timely information, appropriate guidance, reassurance and support—is an integral part of the patient experience.
Shri Nadda congratulated ABVIMS & Dr. RML Hospital for its initiatives on World Patient Safety Day and appreciated its efforts towards strengthening quality and safety through systematic audits, training, continuous monitoring and institutional learning. He said that such efforts contribute to building a healthcare system in which safety, quality, affordability and dignity remain central to every patient’s experience.
Speaking at the Occasion, Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, said that maintaining a clean hospital environment is essential for ensuring safe and quality care. She highlighted that ABVIMS & Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital has achieved NABH accreditation, reflecting its adherence to established standards of patient safety and quality of treatment. She stressed that cleanliness in hospitals cannot be the responsibility of healthcare workers alone and requires active participation from patients, visitors and attendants as well. She said that the convergence of ‘Swachhata Hi Seva’ and World Patient Safety Day provides an opportunity to reinforce collective responsibility towards hygiene, infection prevention and safe healthcare.
Smt. Srivastava highlighted the Government’s continued efforts to make healthcare accessible, affordable and of high quality for every citizen. Referring to the Swasth Nari, Sashakt Parivar campaign launched last year, she noted that more than 17 lakh health camps were organised across the country, with participation of over 11 crore people. She also highlighted key initiatives including Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, the Pradhan Mantri National Dialysis Programme, expansion of vaccination services, PM-ABHIM, eSanjeevani, PM-JAY and Ayushman Vay Vandana, which are strengthening access to preventive and curative healthcare. She further emphasised the importance of affordable medicines in reducing the overall cost of treatment and highlighted the role of Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendras and AMRIT Pharmacies, including the AMRIT Pharmacy at RML Hospital, in improving access to affordable medicines and implants.
Emphasising the importance of patient-centric healthcare, Secretary, Department of Pharmaceuticals, Shri Manoj Joshi said that sustained efforts over the past 10–12 years have focused on improving patient satisfaction and making quality healthcare more accessible, particularly for economically vulnerable sections of society. He highlighted the crucial role of initiatives such as Ayushman Bharat–Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY) and Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) in making quality treatment more accessible and affordable by strengthening financial protection and improving access to affordable medicines. He also underlined that maintaining cleanliness in hospitals remains a significant challenge and called for sustained and collective efforts to strengthen hygiene, cleanliness and infection-control practices, which are integral to ensuring safe and patient-centric care.
Furthermore, A Quality & Safety Handbook of ABVIMS & Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital was also released during the programme. The Handbook provides healthcare staff with practical and standardised operational guidance to support best practices, augment quality of care and strengthen adherence to patient-safety protocols across different operational areas of the hospital.
During the event, Shri Nadda also interacted with the beneficiaries of Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PMJAY) and Jan Ayushadhi Pariyojana.
About Government Efforts for Patient Safety
The Government has been strengthening patient safety through a coordinated approach focused on institutional strengthening, capacity building, knowledge sharing, peer learning and continuous quality improvement. The National Patient Safety Secretariat (NPSS) under the Directorate General of Health Services, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, is facilitating these efforts, including through the India Patient Safety Network (IPSN) comprising 20 AIIMS and 5 Institutes of National Importance (INIs). The Network provides a platform for healthcare institutions to share experiences, identify and disseminate good practices and strengthen patient-safety systems through evidence-based solutions and cross-learning.
The emphasis on learning from institutional experiences and translating them into action was also reflected in the National Conference on Patient Safety 2026, held on 11–12 September 2026 at AIIMS Nagpur. Organised by AIIMS Nagpur in collaboration with NPSS, DGHS and MoHFW, the two-day Conference brought together more than 100 faculty experts and over 450 delegates from medical colleges and healthcare institutions across the country. Senior representatives from various AIIMS and other institutions, along with experts from ICMR, NABH, NABL, AYUSH, National Health Programmes and the Pharmacovigilance Programme of India (PvPI), participated in scientific deliberations and shared institutional innovations and good practices.
The national focus on strengthening patient safety is also being advanced through the National Action Plan for Patient Safety (NAPPS) 2030, being developed through NPSS. Building upon the National Patient Safety Implementation Framework (NPSIF) 2018–25, the proposed framework seeks to strengthen patient safety across healthcare settings, with priority areas including medication, surgical, blood, medical device, laboratory and diagnostic, infection, vaccine and injection, facility and AYUSH patient safety, along with operational research and patient, family and caregiver engagement.
Reflecting this broader approach at the institutional level, ABVIMS & Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital marked World Patient Safety Day by undertaking a month-long, hospital-wide closed-loop audit campaign under the theme, “Measure, Master, Maintain: Elevate Patient Safety at Every Level.” The initiative brought together clinical and operational departments in a structured three-stage process of Baseline Audit, Rapid Corrective Implementation through Training and Verification Audit, with the objective of identifying gaps, undertaking corrective measures and verifying improvements in patient-safety practices.
The focus on patient safety is also complemented by activities undertaken under the Swachhata Hi Seva Abhiyaan, reinforcing the importance of cleanliness, hygiene and well-maintained healthcare environments in creating safe and patient-friendly spaces for patients, families and healthcare workers.
Regular capacity-building initiatives, including master training programmes, orientation of healthcare professionals and patient-safety nodal teams, webinars, institutional sensitisation and technical engagements, are being undertaken to strengthen competencies, promote a culture of safety and support learning from patient-safety incidents.
The Government’s approach is to embed patient safety within routine healthcare delivery, institutional quality improvement and healthcare governance. On World Patient Safety Day, the Ministry reaffirms its commitment to working with States and Union Territories, healthcare institutions, healthcare professionals, patients, families and other stakeholders to strengthen a coordinated and learning-oriented patient-safety ecosystem and ensure safe, timely, coordinated and quality care throughout every patient’s healthcare journey.

ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

content:
Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed amendments to the Drugs Rules, 1945, through Draft Gazette Notification G.S.R. 791 (E) dated 8
th
September 2026, with the objective of strengthening regulatory oversight over Schedule H, H1 and X drugs.
The proposed amendment seeks to address concerns relating to unauthorized access to and sale of Schedule H, H1 and X drugs and recommends mandatory CCTV surveillance at medical stores as an additional regulatory safeguard.
The proposal was initially deliberated upon by the Drugs Consultative Committee (DCC) and was subsequently circulated among the members of the Drugs Technical Advisory Board (DTAB) for deliberation. Following consideration of the proposal, the DTAB recommended its approval.
Upon implementation, the proposed amendment is expected to help strengthen monitoring of the sale and distribution of Schedule H, H1 and X drugs and curb their unauthorized access and sale without valid prescriptions.
The proposed CCTV surveillance mechanism will also enhance transparency and accountability across the pharmaceutical supply chain, thereby strengthening safeguards for public health.
The Ministry has invited objections and suggestions from stakeholders and members of the public on the proposed amendment. Objections and suggestions, if any, may be addressed to the Under Secretary (Drugs), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, U-6, Work Hall-C Wing, First Floor, Kartavya Bhawan-1, New Delhi–110001, or emailed at

title: Union Health Ministry Issues Advisory on Regulation of Stem Cell Therapy
subtitle:
Stem Cell Therapy as Standard Care to be Permitted Only for Disease Conditions/Indications Included in Ministry-Approved List

Therapeutic Use of Stem Cells for Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) Restricted to Clinical Trials with Necessary Regulatory Approvals

Unproven Stem Cell Interventions, Including Stem Cell Therapy for ASD, Not to be Offered as Routine, Standard or Commercial Clinical Services
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                17 SEP 2026 9:18AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Health & Family Welfare has issued an advisory dated 16 September 2026 to all States and Union Territories that have adopted the
Clinical Establishments (Registration and Regulation) Act, 2010
, regarding regulation of stem cell therapy. The advisory has been issued in view of the judgment dated 30 January 2026 of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in
Yash Charitable Trust & Ors. v. Union of India & Ors.
, W.P. (C) No. 369 of 2022 [2026 INSC 96].
The advisory reiterates the existing framework governing stem cell research and therapy and seeks to ensure that
stem cell therapy is permitted as standard care in routine clinical practice only for disease conditions/indications included in the list approved by the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare.
With regard to
Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD)
, the advisory stipulates that the therapeutic use of any type of stem cell in autism is to remain restricted to duly approved clinical trials, in accordance with the
National Guidelines for Stem Cell Research, 2017
, issued jointly by Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) and the Department of Biotechnology (DBT) and other applicable Government instructions issued by the Government of India from time to time.
The Ministry has requested the States and Union Territories to widely disseminate the directions of the Hon’ble Supreme Court to all concerned State and District Regulatory Authorities and Government and private clinical establishments involved in stem cell research, treatment, promotion or administration, for strict compliance with the applicable framework.
The advisory also draws attention to the consequences of non-compliance with the framework governing stem cell therapy. The Hon’ble Supreme Court, in Para 151(xiii) of its judgment dated 30 January 2026, held that non-compliance with the statutory mandate must attract consequences, including professional misconduct under Regulation 7.22 of the IMC Regulations, 2002, as well as action under Sections 32 and 40 of the
Clinical Establishments (Registration and Regulation) Act, 2010
, which provide for cancellation of registration and penalty.
The Ministry has accordingly requested the concerned State and District Regulatory Authorities and clinical establishments to ensure strict compliance with the applicable framework governing stem cell research and therapy.
Reinforcing the regulatory position, the National Medical Commission (NMC), in its advisory dated 5 September 2026, reiterated that stem cell therapy may be offered as standard clinical care only for the approved indications. The advisory further states that unauthorised administration, prescription, promotion or advertisement of stem cell therapy beyond the approved indications would constitute to professional misconduct.
The NMC has further advised State Medical Councils to examine cases of alleged violations brought to their notice and, where professional misconduct by a Registered Medical Practitioner is established after due process, take appropriate disciplinary action in accordance with the applicable statutory and regulatory provisions.

Government committed to Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat@2047

Kumaraswamy appreciated the leadership and vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi in driving India’s transition towards electric mobility and building a cleaner, greener and self-reliant transportation ecosystem. He also appreciated the efforts of the Ministry of Heavy Industries in implementing various initiatives and schemes aimed at accelerating EV adoption, strengthening domestic manufacturing and creating an enabling ecosystem for electric mobility.
Highlighting the Government’s comprehensive approach to electric mobility, Shri H.D. Kumaraswamy spoke about the PM E-DRIVE Scheme, which supports EV adoption and charging infrastructure, as well as the PLI-Auto and PLI-ACC schemes, which are strengthening domestic manufacturing of advanced automotive technologies and battery cells.
The Union Minister emphasised the need for an inclusive, affordable and economically sustainable transition to electric mobility, supported by robust manufacturing, innovation and a strong ecosystem. He congratulated EV users for contributing to cleaner mobility and reduced crude oil imports and appreciated the industry’s efforts towards producing world-class vehicles with increasing local content.
He called upon all stakeholders to work together to build a seamless, accessible and globally competitive electric mobility ecosystem aligned with India’s national mission.
The Union Minister further emphasised the importance of listening to the experiences of EV users and other stakeholders on the ground. He noted that feedback from beneficiaries and distributors would help in further strengthening policy implementation and addressing emerging requirements across different segments of the electric mobility ecosystem.
Industry representatives share perspectives on evolving EV landscape
The programme was also addressed by key representatives from the automobile industry. Mr. Sai Giridhar, President, Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA); Mr. Sushant Naik, Chairman – EMG, Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM); and Mrs. Anjali Singh, President Designate, Automotive Component Manufacturers Association of India (ACMA) shared their perspectives on the evolving electric mobility landscape and the industry’s experience with the growing adoption of electric vehicles.

He highlighted key initiatives including FAME I & II, PLI Auto, PLI-ACC, PM E-DRIVE, PM-eBus Sewa (PSM) and the Rare Earth Permanent Magnet Scheme, and called upon industry to focus on cost competitiveness, technology and global capabilities.
The programme reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to advancing India’s Net Zero goals, promoting Atmanirbhar Bharat, strengthening domestic manufacturing and realising the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047 through the development of a robust, sustainable and self-reliant electric mobility ecosystem.

Swachh Parv, Harit Parv

Swachhata se Samriddhi

and

initiatives

title: Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya Calls for Collective Efforts to Advance Social Justice for a Sustainable Future
subtitle:
Economic Growth and Social Progress Must Move Together: Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya at the Global Coalition for Social Justice Annual Forum 2026

Union Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya Sets Out Three Priorities for the Global Coalition for Social Justice

Global Coalition for Social Justice Annual Forum 2026 Brings Together Global Partners to Advance Social Justice and Decent Work; India Takes Over Co-Chairmanship
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                17 SEP 2026 1:59PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Global Coalition for Social Justice Annual Forum 2026 is being held virtually on 16–17 September 2026, bringing together governments, employers’ and workers’ organisations, international and regional organisations, development institutions, the private sector, academia and civil society to strengthen cooperation and accelerate collective action for social justice and decent work. The Official Opening of the Forum was graced by Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, Union Minister for Labour & Employment and Youth Affairs & Sports, Mr. Gilbert F. Houngbo, Director-General, International Labour Organization (ILO), Ms Jacqueline Mugo, President, International Organisation of Employers; Mr Luc Triangle, General Secretary, International Trade Union Confederation and Mr Luiz Marinho, Minister of Labour and Employment, Brazil.
Addressing the gathering, Union Minister, Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, called for collective efforts to place social justice at the heart of endeavours, in order to build a more inclusive, resilient and sustainable future. The shared objective of the global community, the Minister said, should be to translate cooperation into opportunities, growth into shared prosperity and commitments to social justice into tangible change. He said India brings to the Forum its experience of delivering transformation at scale and its commitment to building a more inclusive world of work. Emphasising the need for economic growth and social progress to move together, the Minister said that growth must create decent jobs, technology must promote inclusion and innovation must contribute to improving people’s lives.
Dr. Mandaviya said that India is preparing for the future of work through technology, skills and international cooperation. He underlined that the changing world of work requires renewed focus on skills, employability and labour mobility. In this context, he highlighted India’s partnership with the ILO to pilot an International Reference Classification of Occupations across India, Brazil and Germany to support smoother international mobility. He also referred to the New Delhi Declaration 2026 adopted under India’s BRICS Presidency and the BRICS CONNECT initiative, as well as the consensus on an International Digital Platform for Remote Employment to create new virtual employment opportunities for youth across the Global South.
Highlighting India’s reform-led approach, the Minister said that the country continues to focus on transformative reforms, targeted welfare and digital innovation, ensuring that the benefits of economic growth reach the last mile. He drew attention to the consolidation of 29 central labour laws into four modern Labour Codes, stating that the reforms strengthen workers’ protection while creating an enabling environment for enterprises. He also noted that India has become one of the leading countries to provide legal recognition to gig and platform workers. Dr. Mandaviya further emphasised the role of sustained reforms and digital delivery in expanding social protection, noting that India’s social protection coverage has increased from 19 per cent in 2015 to 68.4 per cent in 2026, bringing more than one billion people within the social protection framework.
The Minister highlighted the role of Digital Public Infrastructure in strengthening social protection delivery. He said that the e-Shram portal, with nearly 320 million registered unorganised workers, is the world’s largest digital database of its kind and connects workers with welfare schemes across national and State Governments. Referring to the National Career Service (NCS), he said that the platform connects jobseekers with domestic and international opportunities, with India also sharing the NCS framework with Mauritius.
Dr. Mandaviya said that India stands ready to deepen partnerships across the Global South in areas including digital public infrastructure, social protection, skills and employment services. He said that sharing successful experiences can help translate national achievements into shared progress and reiterated India’s commitment to strengthening the voice of South-South Cooperation in shaping the future of work and advancing social justice. He also noted that as India assumes the Co-Chairmanship of the Coalition’s Coordinating Group, it would build on the leadership provided by Brazil during the important phase of the Coalition.
As Co-Chair, Dr. Mandaviya outlined three priorities for the Coalition. First, he called for translating collective commitments into action at the country level, in line with national priorities and circumstances. Second, he emphasised the need to strengthen knowledge and experience sharing, intensify cooperation and bring more enterprises into the social justice agenda. Third, he stressed that social justice should inform the choices that shape development beyond 2030. He said that with more than 400 partners, the Coalition has unique collective strength, while its objective should not be to prescribe one pathway for all, but to ensure that social justice remains an integral part of the choices countries make about their future.
Dr. Mandaviya reaffirmed India’s commitment to working with all members to make the Global Coalition for Social Justice a strong platform for international cooperation, shared learning and practical action.
Background
The Global Coalition for Social Justice, established by ILO in 2023, is a global platform aimed at strengthening multistakeholder cooperation and accelerating collective action for decent work and social justice. With more than 400 partners comprising governments, employers’ and workers’ organisations, international and regional organisations, development banks, the private sector, academia and civil society, the Coalition seeks to promote coherent and integrated approaches to advance social justice, expand opportunities, foster shared prosperity and contribute to resilient societies.
The Global Coalition for Social Justice Annual Forum 2026 is being held virtually on 16–17 September 2026, ahead of the High-Level General Debate of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly. The Forum provides a platform for partners to share experiences and lessons learned, review progress, identify opportunities for collaboration and shape future collective action.

KVIC Disburses ₹289 Crore Margin Money Subsidy to 3,366 PMEGP Beneficiaries; Five Digital Initiatives Launched
date:

content:
The Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC), Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India, inaugurated the "Seva Sankalp, Khadi Mahotsav 2026" on Thursday, marking the birth anniversary of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, from the KVIC campus at Gandhi Darshan, Rajghat. The commemoration will be celebrated nationwide from September 17 to October 17, 2026, with public participation. The chief guest, Shri Manoj Goyal, Chairman, KVIC, inaugurated the event. On the occasion, former Delhi Mayor Shri Jai Prakash, representatives of Khadi institutions, artisans, PMEGP beneficiaries, trainees, officers and employees of KVIC, as well as artisans and other participants who joined online from across the country, were present. During the event, the artisans cut a cake with #AshirwadKaDiya and lit 25 lamps of "Sankalp se Siddhi" to symbolize Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's 25 years of service, good governance, and public participation.
Shri Goyal said that service, good governance, and public participation have been key principles ​​in Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's 25 years of public life. Inspired by this spirit, KVIC will spread the message of Khadi, Swadeshi, employment, and self-reliance through the 'Seva Sankalp, Khadi Mahotsav-2026'. He said that Khadi is not just a fabric, but a symbol of self-respect, employment, rural economy, and Swadeshi. Under the Prime Minister's leadership, campaigns like 'Vocal for Local', 'Atmanirbhar Bharat', and 'Local to Global' have given a new identity to local products and rural entrepreneurship.
During the programme, machines and toolkits were distributed to artisans from Delhi and the North East regions. Shri Goyal said that these are not just equipment, but new opportunities for employment, self-reliance, and respect for artisans. Margin money subsidy of ₹289 crore was also disbursed under the PMEGP. This will establish 3,366 new projects across the country and create employment opportunities for approximately 37,026 people. Bank loans worth approximately ₹873 crore have been provided for these projects. At the event, 5,000 new PMEGP units were launched online. He said the objective of PMEGP is to transform youth, women, and rural entrepreneurs from job seekers to job creators.
The program marked the launch of the E-Commerce Portal, PMEGP Online EDP Portal, PMEGP Online EDP Mobile App, Hindi Vaibhav Portal, and KVIC Digital 2.0, aimed at making KVIC's digital services more accessible and effective. Also, 760 individual, group workshops, and renovated stores were inaugurated online across the country, and a Khadi and Village Industries Exhibition was organized. Activities such as the inauguration of a selfie point, a live demonstration of spinning the charkha, and the "Swadeshi Sankalp" campaign were also organized at the venue. Certificates were distributed to candidates trained in various skill development courses. Cleanliness activities were organized at the KVIC office complex at Gandhi Darshan, and Chairman, KVIC, Shri Manoj Goyal, planted a sapling, promoting environmental protection and a clean campus.
Under the "Seva Sankalp, Khadi Mahotsav 2026," cleanliness drives, tree plantations, Khadi Yatras, the Swadeshi Sankalp pledge, awareness programs, artisan dialogues, and training programs will be organized across the country til 17th  October. Schools, villages, towns and Khadi institutions will be associated to these activities. Shri Goyal said that KVIC's effort is that this festival should not remain just a departmental programme but should become a campaign for the people and a festival of public participation. He said that there should be dialogue of Khadi in every school, talk of village industries in every village, talk of Swadeshi in every market.
Seva Sankalp, Khadi Mahotsav will also be linked with the 'Swachhata Hi Seva 2026' campaign running from 17th September to 17th October. This year the theme of Swachhata Hi Seva campaign is 'Participation in Cleanliness, Clean India, Developed India'. Shri Goyal said, "Cleanliness is service, Swadeshi is service, providing employment is service, and respecting artisans is service." He called upon artisans, Khadi institutions, PMEGP beneficiaries, youth, and the KVIC family across the country to actively participate in the "Seva Sankalp, Khadi Mahotsav 2026."
On this occasion, Shri Manoj Goyal opined that under the guidance of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Khadi has achieved a new dimension. Today, Khadi has become a powerful medium to realize the resolve of Atmanirbhar Bharat, Vocal for Local, Local to Global, and Developed India 2047. He said that Khadi is not just a fabric, but a source of livelihood for millions of artisans and weavers, a symbol of India's cultural heritage and sustainable development.
Khadi and Village Industries sector has made unprecedented progress due to  Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's visionary thoughtfulness and policies, he added.  In the financial year 2025-26, the turnover of the Khadi and Village Industries sector exceeded ₹1.87 lakh crore, while the total income generated through this sector was ₹1.87 lakh crore. content:
Under the joint aegis of the Union Ministry of Panchayati Raj and the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, a special interaction program with beneficiaries of the 'SVAMITVA' Scheme and Fisheries Scheme, as well as a property card distribution ceremony under the SVAMITVA scheme, was held today at the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) Auditorium in Anand.
Union Minister of Panchayati Raj, Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh was specially present as the Chief Guest, and Union Minister of State for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Prof. S. P. Singh Baghel was present as the Special Guest on this occasion.
Speaking at the program, Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh stated that the entire life of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has been dedicated to the service of Mother India. During his successful tenure as the Chief Minister of Gujarat, he accomplished the monumental task of bringing Narmada waters to every corner, permanently solving the state's major water problem. It was due to this journey of development and popularity that the people of the country entrusted him with the leadership of the nation in 2014. Today, under the Prime Minister's leadership, India is moving forward with the resolve to become a 'Viksit Bharat' by 2047. The Central Government is committed to the equitable development of every region and state of the country. Uniting all states into a single thread without any political discrimination to make the country self-reliant is the main objective of the Prime Minister.
The Union Minister further stated that property-related issues were the biggest cause of violence and disputes in rural areas. Owing to the Prime Minister's foresight, the 'SVAMITVA Scheme' was launched, under which title deeds (cards) for their land/properties are handed over to villagers through drone surveys. title: India Calls for Secure, Affordable and Reliable Energy at the G20 Energy Abundance Ministerial Meeting in USA
subtitle:
G20 Advances Key Outcomes on Clean Cooking, Permitting and Critical Minerals

Union Minister Shri Manohar Lal underscored India’s commitment to building a resilient and future-ready energy system, supported by efficient regulation and secure critical mineral supply chains
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                17 SEP 2026 11:43AM by PIB Delhi
content:
Shri Manohar Lal, Union Minister for Power and Housing & Urban Affairs, led the Indian delegation at the G20 Energy Abundance Ministerial Meeting held in Houston, USA, from 14-16 September 2026, under the U.S. G20 Presidency. He participated in discussions across three thematic pillars: Energy Security and Affordable Baseload; Permitting and Regulatory Efficiency; and Critical Minerals & Resilient Supply Chains.
During his interventions, the Union Minister emphasised that secure, affordable and reliable energy is essential for development, particularly for developing economies. He stressed the importance of international cooperation and leveraging the complementarities among countries to advance the common good of all, while respecting diverse national circumstances and development priorities.
He highlighted that India is building a resilient and future-ready energy system that is increasingly digital, decentralised and consumer-centric. He also underlined India’s significant progress in the power sector, with installed electricity generation capacity reaching 552 GW, of which more than half is from non-fossil fuel sources. He further highlighted India’s early achievement of key NDC targets and its long-term goal of achieving Net Zero by 2070.
The Minister highlighted the range of reforms undertaken by India to strengthen regulatory efficiency, encourage competition and facilitate greater participation and investment across the energy sector. He showcased initiatives such as the National Single Window System, PARIVESH and PM Gati Shakti, which have helped improve predictability and streamline approvals for infrastructure development.
On critical minerals, the Minister emphasized the importance of secure, resilient and diversified supply chains, stressing circularity and downstream value creation in developing countries. He also highlighted India’s National Critical Mineral Mission, covering the value chain from exploration to recycling, and called for G20 cooperation on recycling, recovery and diversification.
The Ministerial Meeting resulted in a number of important outcomes across the three pillars, including:
(i) Clean Cooking Access: The G20 Statement on Advancing Clean Cooking Access underscored universal access to clean cooking and promoted a technology-neutral and nationally appropriate approach, recognizing that no single solution could meet the diverse needs of all countries. It identified LPG as an important clean-cooking pathway, particularly for developing countries, and called for equitable access to financing for all clean-cooking solutions, including projects deploying LPG.
(ii) Permitting and Regulatory Efficiency: The G20 Permitting and Regulatory Efficiency Symposium recognized the importance of efficient and streamlined permitting and regulatory processes for facilitating energy infrastructure development, while encouraging cooperation through voluntary information exchange, capacity building, and digital and AI-enabled tools.
(iii) Water Reuse: The G20 Water Reuse Initiative was advanced as a voluntary framework to promote science- and evidence-based, cost-effective fit-for-purpose water reuse in line with national policies. It encouraged cooperation and exchange of best practices to strengthen water security and resilience, while recognizing that there is no one-size-fits-all approach.
(iv) Critical Minerals: The G20 Critical Minerals Meeting Communiqué recognized the importance of critical minerals for energy security, digital infrastructure, emerging technologies and economic development. It emphasised collaborative and voluntary cooperation respecting national sovereignty and diverse domestic pathways, while promoting innovation, circularity, investment and international cooperation for diversification, value addition and resilient supply chains.
On the sidelines of the Ministerial Meeting, the Minister also held bilateral meetings with Mr. Chris Wright, Secretary, U.S. Department of Energy; Mr. Doug Burgum, Secretary, U.S. Department of the Interior; and Mr. Corey Hogan, Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Energy and Natural Resources, Canada. The discussions covered a range of areas of mutual interest, including resilient energy infrastructure and supply chains, power sector transformation, and India’s plans for meeting the growing energy requirements of its digital economy.
The Minister’s participation in the G20 Energy Abundance Ministerial Meeting underscores India’s constructive contribution to the global energy discourse and its continued commitment to building a secure, sustainable, affordable and inclusive energy future for all.

title: NHAI Rajmargyatra App Hosts ‘OneTag’ FASTag Portability Service
subtitle: Availability of ‘OneTag’ FASTag portability has expanded the citizen centric services available for National Highway users on Rajmargyatra Mobile App
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                17 SEP 2026 4:15PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In order to enhance consumer choice for FASTag users, ‘OneTag
’
- a FASTag portability service is now available on National Highways Authority of India (NHAI)
Rajmargyatra
App. The initiative enables FASTag users to change their issuer while retaining the existing FASTag affixed to their vehicle, eliminating the need to obtain a new physical tag. The availability of ‘OneTag’ FASTag portability has expanded citizen centric services available for National Highway users on
Rajmargyatra
App, which include FASTag Annual Pass, FASTag Local Pass, Emergency Helpline 1033 among other services.
The Rajmargyatra
app guides users through the FASTag portability process. FASTag users can login to App and enter their vehicle registration number to check eligibility. The user will receive a verification six-digit Mobile Verification Code (MVC) from current issuer bank. Following authorization, the user will be required to select a new issuer, complete customer verification and wallet onboarding with the new issuer to complete the portability process. Following successful portability, the existing FASTag ID linked to vehicle registration number will remain unchanged, allowing users to continue using the same physical tag with a different issuer bank.
After portability is completed, previous issuer will close the existing FASTag wallet and refund the available balance, post applicable adjustments. Also, interoperable FASTag has a cooling period of 6 months before it can be ported again.
The ‘OneTag
’
initiative will help to improve FASTag lifecycle management by reducing the need for repeated tag production, thereby lowering operational costs, dispatching and reissuance expenses. ‘OneTag’ will also help to streamline the issuer-switching journey, enhance customer choice and contribute to a more interoperable and efficient FASTag ecosystem.
With a penetration rate of over 98 percent and around 13 crore users, FASTag has revolutionized the Electronic Toll Collection system in the country. The introduction of ‘OneTag’ will further strengthen the digital tolling architecture and provide FASTag users with greater flexibility, while retaining the existing physical tag and proving greater convenience to the National Highway users.

date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                17 SEP 2026 4:18PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Rural Development and Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, today planted saplings with sarpanches and departmental officials at the Pusa campus in New Delhi on the occasion of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s birthday and extended his birthday greetings to the Prime Minister. Thereafter, the Union Minister addressed the National Workshop organised on Viksit Bharat–G RAM G. The workshop was attended by elected representatives of Panchayati Raj Institutions, Commissioners and senior officials of States and Union Territories, and other participants.
­­­­
On the occasion, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan directed officials to conduct random inspections of works being undertaken under the scheme. Where works are being carried out in accordance with the prescribed standards and procedures, the concerned persons should be appreciated. However, wherever any irregularity is found, strict action should be taken at the very outset so that no one dares to violate the rules in future.
There Will Be No Leniency in Case of Fraud
Union Minister for Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan issued a strong message to the States and Union Territories regarding any kind of fraud and irregularity under the Viksit Bharat–G RAM G Scheme. He said that fraud in the scheme would not be tolerated at any cost.
Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said, “Remember, we will not allow any fraud in this scheme at any cost. I am clearly saying as the Minister that if there is any fraud, no one will be spared. Action will be taken against anyone who indulges in irregularities.” He said that if a pond in a village is already full and workers are still being engaged there, it is a matter that needs to be investigated. He directed officials to keep a close watch on such cases.
Conduct Random Inspections of Works; Take Action at the Very Outset if Irregularities Are Found
Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan told officials of States and Union Territories that only two months have passed since the scheme was launched and the third month is underway. Therefore, it is essential to keep the monitoring and inspection mechanism strong right from the beginning. He directed that random inspections of selected works be conducted. Where works are being carried out properly, the concerned persons should be appreciated, while any irregularity found should invite immediate action so that irregularities are curbed at the initial stage and such situations do not recur in future.
Technology Will Help Curb Fraud
The Union Minister said that technology has been used in the scheme to ensure better monitoring of works and to leave no scope for fraud. He said that attendance of workers has now been made mandatory through Face Authentication. Therefore, it should also be ensured through the technological system that there are no gaps in this mechanism.
He said that when a complaint comes to light, it is natural to be concerned. He urged all concerned officials to ensure that no breach occurs at any level in the implementation of the scheme. He said, “All the officials are sitting here, and I want to tell them and the Commissioners to ensure that no one is able to breach the system at any cost.”
Ensure Work for Workers; They Should Not Remain Without Work Even for an Hour
Union Minister for Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that the most important objective of the scheme is to provide employment to workers. He said that workers should get work and should not remain without work even for an hour. He also emphasised that timely payment of wages must be ensured. He said that works permitted under the rules should be undertaken after following the prescribed procedures.
He also emphasised adherence to the wage-material ratio under the scheme. He said that at the district level, 60 per cent of the funds are to be spent on wages and 40 per cent on material. Officials were directed to follow the rules and prescribed procedures and prioritise works that create durable and useful assets in villages.
Work Does Not Mean Merely Digging Soil and Dumping It Elsewhere
The Union Minister said that work does not mean merely digging soil at one place and dumping it at another. Keeping in view the objective of “ViksitGaon for a Viksit Bharat”, works under the Viksit Bharat–G RAM G Scheme should be considered in a manner that creates a strong foundation for development in villages and strengthens the rural economy.
He told officials that there is now a need to consider how the Viksit Bharat–G RAM G Scheme can contribute to building ViksitGaon. Along with providing employment, the scheme should facilitate the creation of assets that remain useful to rural communities over the long term and help make villages self-reliant and developed.
Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that the success of the scheme can be ensured only when workers receive adequate employment, transparency is maintained in the execution of works, fraud is completely curbed, and the scheme also contributes to building developed villages alongside a developed India.
National Service Is the Core Mantra of PM Modi’s Life
Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that today is a highly relevant and special day. There is an atmosphere of joy and celebration across the country. Today is the birthday of our Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi. On this occasion, he extended heartfelt greetings and best wishes to the Prime Minister on behalf of rural India.
He said, “My only prayer to God is that Prime Minister Narendra Modi ji may be blessed with a long and healthy life and may he continue to serve the country and its people in the same manner.” He said that national service has remained the core mantra of the Prime Minister’s life.
He said that his journey of public service as the head of government for 25 consecutive years is significant in itself. He served as the Chief Minister of Gujarat and is now leading the nation as the Prime Minister. This long and continuous journey of service is a noteworthy chapter in the history of Indian democracy.
He said that under the leadership of the Prime Minister, the vision of a new India is taking shape—an India that is prosperous, glorious, strong, self-reliant and developed.

title: Science Policy and Communication in an Era of Global Challenges: From Boundaries to Breakthroughs
date:

content:
Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) has been organizing annual sessions (virtual mode) during the Science Summit at United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) that are aimed at showcasing CSIR's contributions to Science and Technology and efforts towards Global Sustainable Development. The central theme of SSUNGA81 is "From
Boundaries to Breakthroughs: Science for a Regenerative and Equitable Future
". With this background, CSIR-NIScPR organised an online
session on
“Science Policy and Communication in an Era of Global Challenges: From Boundaries to Breakthroughs”
on 16 September 2026, bringing together experts and practitioners to deliberate on strengthening the interface between science, policy and society in addressing complex global challenges.
Dr. Naresh Kumar, Chief Scientist, CSIR-NIScPR, in his welcome address emphasized the importance of moving scientific knowledge from research to real-world application and urged the need for stronger institutional mechanisms for connecting research, policy and deployment.
Outlining the overview of the scientific session, Dr. Kasturi Mandal, Senior Principal Scientist, CSIR-NIScPR and convener of the session mentioned the persistent global “science divide” in infrastructure, skills and participation and that the central premise of the session is that science policy and science communication are complementary pillars of sustainable & inclusive development.
Dr. (Mrs.) Geetha Vani Rayasam, Director, CSIR-National Institute of Science Communication and Policy Research (CSIR-NIScPR) chaired the scientific session. She also highlighted the significance of technology readiness, scientific entrepreneurship and foresight on emerging technologies, particularly in view of rapid developments in Artificial Intelligence. She stressed the need to anticipate emerging scenarios and strengthen evidence-informed policy approaches to ensure that scientific and technological advances translate into meaningful societal outcomes.
Shri Rohit Gupta, CTO of the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India, presented TRL Compass, India's evidence-based national framework for assessing technology readiness, showing how a structured, sector-specific approach can de-risk deep tech investment and offer a template that emerging economies can adapt to their own priorities. He highlighted the collaboration between the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser (PSA) and CSIR-NIScPR in development of sectoral specific TRL assessment frameworks for India which could be relevant to global south.
Dr. Joana Ball, Managing Director, Directory of Open Access Journals surged the involvement of governments, funders, researchers, universities, libraries, and publishers in strengthening open knowledge systems. She also highlighted the role of CSIR-NIScPR in connecting Indian research with researchers and wider society.
Dr. Avinash Kshitij, Scientist, CSIR-NIScPR highlighted aligning technological development with societal needs, investment, skills, and market readiness, highlighting technology foresight to anticipate emerging trends and policy priorities. Research shows startups and entrepreneurship can address societal issues through emerging technologies.
Dr. Vinayak, Scientist, CSIR-NIScPR highlighted a complexity-based approach that goes beyond citation counts to identify breakthrough research by exploiting the local structure of citation networks, map which countries are making breakthroughs in which disciplines, and reveal the scientific capabilities of nations.
Dr. Paramananda Barman, Scientist, CSIR-NIScPR discussed the relevance of inclusive science communication, highlighting the barriers such as language, literacy, culture and digital access, approaches and contributions of CSIR-NIScPR for strengthening SciComm.

title: S&T based community initiative improves detection and control of TB in Rajasthan
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                17 SEP 2026 3:32PM by PIB Delhi
content:
A new, scientific data-based community driven initiative has dramatically improved TB detection and control in remote, underserved regions of Rajasthan.
Tuberculosis continues to be a major public health problem in many remote areas like the tribal districts of Rajasthan. Factors such as difficult terrain, low awareness, social stigma, seasonal migration, and delayed diagnosis have long hindered TB control efforts and led to TB burden.
In order to address this, AIIMS Jodhpur conducted Cluster based population survey, active case finding, laboratory confirmation to estimate the burden of TB (Active and Latent) among the tribal population and their anti-TB drug resistance pattern.
The study has found ways to limit transmission of TB in the tribal districts of southern Rajasthan, through early detection and streamlining patients to undergo preventive screening through community participation and reaching out with timely treatment.
Fig
: Filed work- screening, sputum collection, Transport and health awareness
With support from the SEED division of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), they conducted Household survey, symptom screening, sputum testing, NTEP diagnostics and data analysis among more than 6000 people from Sirohi, Udaipur, Chittorgarh, Dungarpur, Pratapgarh and Banswara districts.
The researchers led by Dr Shoban Babu Varthya (Additional Professor), Department of Pharmacology AIIMS Jodhpur conducted workshops to sensitize people and combined epidemiological survey, grass root level participation of Healthcare workers (HCWs) and panchayat people to improve early detection. Active case finding laboratory confirmation was also undertaken.
People with symptoms of tuberculosis and those with positive results were identified and given treatment for TB as per national guidelines. Besides, community awareness was generated to improve the understanding of TB to help limit the transmission of TB through early detection and streamlining patients to undergo preventive screening among household contacts. This helped enable implementation of TB Mukt Panchayat model with the use of scientific data.
This initiative demonstrates how targeted, scientific research can generate actionable data that directly informs policy and strengthens TB control in vulnerable populations.

₹1 Lakh Crore RDI Scheme Opens New Pathways for Private-Sector R&D and Deep-Tech Innovation: Dr. Jitendra Singh
